Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- The failing test overrides the mean computation in SummaryStatistics:
  - stats.setMeanImpl(new Mean());
  - Then it adds values and compares stats.getMean() with new Mean().evaluate(scores).

- Relevant code paths:
  - SummaryStatistics.setMeanImpl(StorelessUnivariateStatistic) simply assigns the provided implementation after ensuring no data have been added.
  - SummaryStatistics.getMean() returns meanImpl.getResult().
  - SummaryStatistics.addValue(double) updates internal aggregates:
    - Always increments secondMoment (which internally also maintains first moment).
    - Only increments meanImpl if it is not an instance of Mean:
      if (!(meanImpl instanceof Mean)) { meanImpl.increment(value); }
  - Mean() constructor creates an independent FirstMoment (incMoment = true; moment = new FirstMoment()).

- Step-by-step failure mechanism in the test:
  1. stats.setMeanImpl(new Mean()) installs a Mean that maintains its own independent FirstMoment (not wired to SummaryStatistics.secondMoment).
  2. For each added value, addValue increments secondMoment but does not call meanImpl.increment(value), because meanImpl is an instance of Mean.
  3. As a result, the installed Mean’s internal FirstMoment remains untouched (n = 0), so meanImpl.getResult() yields NaN (or an uninitialized result).
  4. stats.getMean() returns that NaN, which does not match new Mean().evaluate(scores), causing the assertion to fail.

- Connection to the current bug report about setVarianceImpl leading to NaN standard deviation:
  - addValue similarly only increments varianceImpl if it is not an instance of Variance:
    if (!(varianceImpl instanceof Variance)) { varianceImpl.increment(value); }
  - When users call stats.setVarianceImpl(new Variance(true/false)), the provided Variance is a standalone instance not wired to SummaryStatistics’ internal SecondMoment. Because it is an instance of Variance, addValue will not increment it, leaving it uninitialized; thus varianceImpl.getResult() (and consequently getStandardDeviation()) becomes NaN.

- Root cause:
  - The code relies on a type-based heuristic: “if it’s Mean/Variance, it must be using the shared internal moment, so don’t increment it here.”
  - This assumption holds only for the default Mean/Variance that are constructed to share SummaryStatistics’ internal SecondMoment. It fails for arbitrary user-supplied Mean/Variance instances (like new Mean() or new Variance(true/false)) which manage their own moments unless explicitly wired.
  - Therefore, overriding with a standard Mean or Variance breaks because addValue suppresses incrementing those implementations, leaving them uninitialized and leading to NaN results.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
